gap: No result ChatGPT got says how each 1,000 Wh unit is switched into its quiet charging rate. The DJI Power 1000 V2 has a physical charging-speed switch on the unit. The quiet or low rate on the BLUETTI AC180, Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 and Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 is set in the maker's phone app; their pages and guides describe no on-unit control. The measured quiet figures ChatGPT quoted (AC180 Silent about 37 dB, C1000 Gen 2 fans off at 200 W) are only reached once the shopper has set the lower rate in the app.
standout_why: I compared our own page (dealectric.com/quietest-1000wh-power-station-while-charging), thepowerstationguide.com's noise guide and voltandvalley.com's 'Are Portable Power Stations Loud?'. Our page says only 'set the lowest AC charge rate in the app before bed' and does not say how this works on each model. thepowerstationguide says only that Anker 'exposes AC recharge speed in its app' and does not say how Jackery's Quiet Mode is selected. voltandvalley says only that 'several brands expose a charge-speed setting in their app' and names no models. None of the three mentions DJI's physical switch. None says that BLUETTI's Silent mode exists only in the app, or that the Anker's plain AC charging rate is 1,200 W. All three explain the heat-and-fan mechanism (faster charging means more heat, so the fan runs harder), so that part is not new.
decides: This confirms rather than flips the pick. The DJI Power 1000 V2 is the only candidate where the shopper can choose the slower rate on the unit itself; on the rest the slow rate goes through the phone app. The DJI is also the unit measured at about 37 dB at full speed. For a shopper who wants a quiet overnight charge without depending on an app (an RV with no signal, or a non-technical user), the DJI pick gets stronger. The AC180 and C1000 Gen 2 recommendations need a caveat: their quiet figures depend on first setting Silent or a low AC rate in the app. If that isn't done, the Anker charges at up to 1,200 W by Anker's own spec. Our page does not have the AC180's default rate from an opened source.

findings.label: How the charging speed is chosen
findings.value: Physical switch on the unit: 'physical switch for charging speed' that lets you 'toggle between faster and slower charging right on the unit'
findings.note: This is a named reviewer, not the maker. The DJI US store and dji.com support/FAQ pages redirected to an account page or 404, so I could not confirm the switch in DJI's own words. DroneXL also says the companion app adjusts 'charge limits and timeouts' but does not say it sets charge speed.

findings.label: Full-speed wall charging rate
findings.note: Reviewer's own measurement. The review gives no dB number; it says 'The fan barely makes a sound' during full-speed charging.

findings.label: How Silent charging mode is enabled
findings.value: App only: '*Set up this mode on BLUETTI App for a silent charging.'
findings.note: This is BLUETTI's footnote under its Silent Charging Mode section. The same page claims 'as low as 45dB while charging' and Turbo 'up to 1440W input, goes from 0 to 80% in just 45 minutes'. It gives no wattage for Silent mode.

findings.label: How the AC recharge speed is set
findings.value: In the Anker app: 'UltraFast Recharging must be activated via the Anker app'; the app section lists 'Set AC Recharging Speed'
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen2 product page (US)
findings.note: The page describes no on-unit control for charging speed. Spec table: 'AC Power (Charging) 1,200W Max'; 'AC Power (UltraFast Charging)' 1,600 W. The only dB claim is 'Quietly Discharges at 20 dB Under 200W', which is for output, not charging. So reaching the reviewer's 200 W fans-off rate means lowering the rate in the app.

findings.label: How silent charging and emergency charging are set
findings.value: Through the Jackery App: you can 'remotely schedule silent charging modes' via the app; 'Emergency Charging via App: 1H'; standard 'AC Adapter: 1.7H'
findings.source_title: Jackery AU – Ultimate Guide to Using Jackery 1000 v2
findings.note: This is Jackery's own (AU) guide. The only buttons it describes are power, AC and DC, with no on-unit charging-mode control. It lists 'Less than 22dB' as 'Quiet Level' without saying the figure is for charging. The US product page returned HTTP 429.
